archetypes.pitch: A four-to-five color midrange deck that rewards controlling many basic land types. Ten typed duals and Thran Portal turn on payoffs like Leyline Binding and Herd Migration that scale with your Domain. For players who love ramping into powerful, splashy value.
archetypes.rationale: Payoffs at every rarity scale with basic land types while ten typed taplands, Thran Portal and Timeless Lotus provide the fixing.

archetypes.pitch: A ramp deck that floods the board with mana and spends it on scaling spells. Kicker and X-cost cards like Shivan Devastator get bigger the more mana you have, and Volshe Tideturner helps pay for it all. For players who like starting small and ending enormous.
archetypes.rationale: 50 kicker/X cards reward extra mana; any-color ramp and Volshe Tideturner's kicked-spell mana fund the payoffs.

archetypes.pitch: A black midrange deck that grinds value from dying creatures. Braids, Arisen Nightmare and Nemata, Primeval Warden reward sacrifice while cheap recursive bodies keep the engine fed. For players who enjoy trading, draining, and outlasting the opponent.
archetypes.rationale: Death payoffs, sacrifice outlets and recursive fodder all have real depth; Tyrannical Pitlord and Defiler of Flesh join on oracle text.

archetypes.pitch: A white-based aggro deck that builds a wide army and pumps it. Valiant Veteran and King Darien XLVIII act as lords over token-makers in every color for explosive attacks. For players who like flooding the board and swinging as a team.
archetypes.rationale: Soldier-token makers in five colors feed lords and width payoffs; enlist creatures want the same spare bodies.

archetypes.pitch: A tempo-aggro deck that rewards casting instants and sorceries. Balmor, Battlemage Captain and a squad of Wizards grow and burn as you chain cheap spells. For players who love a hyperactive, spell-slinging playstyle.
archetypes.rationale: Five separate instant/sorcery cast triggers plus engine rares; cheap kicker instants double as spell count.

archetypes.pitch: A UB control-tempo deck where your graveyard is a resource. Tolarian Terror and Haughty Djinn get cheaper and bigger as spells and creatures pile up in the yard. For players who like efficient interaction backed by a growing bin.
archetypes.rationale: Payoffs count instants/sorceries or creatures in the graveyard while genuine mill enablers fill it.

archetypes.pitch: A GW deck that snowballs the board with permanent counters. Defiler of Vigor pumps every green creature you cast and kicked payoffs keep stacking counters. For players who like a steady, growing beatdown.
archetypes.rationale: Defiler of Vigor mass-pumps every green permanent spell; kicked counter creatures and counter tricks stack the rest.

archetypes.pitch: A classic control deck with sweepers, taxes, and clean finishers. Temporary Lockdown and Drag to the Bottom reset the board before Sheoldred or another bomb takes over. For players who like answering everything and winning late.
archetypes.rationale: Real sweepers, taxing pieces, instant-speed draw and clean finishers make classic draft control fully buildable.

archetypes.pitch: A midrange deck that turns cheap artifacts into an engine. Jhoira and Meria draw cards and make mana off your trinkets while Karn ramps and rewards density. For players who enjoy value machines built from small parts.
archetypes.rationale: Meria and Jhoira are true engines fed by the cube's cheap nontoken artifact bodies; Karn ramps and pays off density.

archetypes.pitch: A WB midrange deck that converts incidental life gain into advantage. Shanna, Purifying Blade draws off the life you gain while Sheoldred punishes the opponent's own draws. For players who like a steady, resilient grind.
archetypes.rationale: Shanna converts life gained into cards and Knight of Dawn's Light amplifies the cube's abundant incidental gain.

archetypes.pitch: A BRG deck that treats lands in the graveyard as fuel. Soul of Windgrace and Uurg, Spawn of Turg turn discarded and dead lands into value and threats. For players who love recursion and grinding resources.
archetypes.rationale: Soul of Windgrace discards and retrieves lands while Uurg counts them; Serra Paragon replays lands from the graveyard.

archetypes.pitch: A UW value deck that reuses enter-the-battlefield effects. Golden Argosy mass-blinks your crew each combat to re-trigger cards like Aether Channeler. For players who enjoy chaining ETB triggers for relentless advantage.
archetypes.rationale: Golden Argosy mass-blinks its crew every combat, re-buying the cube's dense ETB effects.

archetypes.pitch: A green tribal deck built on the cube's biggest tribe. Leaf-Crowned Visionary pumps and draws off every Elf you cast, backed by mana Elves that go wide fast. For players who like snowballing a synergistic creature army.
archetypes.rationale: Sixteen Elves - the largest tribe - behind a lord that pumps and draws off every Elf spell.

archetypes.pitch: A fast red tribe with a sacrifice twist. Rundvelt Hordemaster is both a lord and a death payoff while Squee keeps coming back for more. For players who want aggressive, disposable creatures that still generate value.
archetypes.rationale: Hordemaster is lord and death payoff in one; Squee recurs himself; Defiler of Instinct pays off red-permanent density.

archetypes.pitch: A five-color deck that turns a wall of legendary creatures into an engine. Jodah, the Unifier and Ratadrabik of Urborg convert your legends into extra bodies and card advantage. For players who like a legendary all-star lineup.
archetypes.rationale: 48 legendary creatures give Jodah and Ratadrabik constant material, with legend-only mana and equipment as support.

archetypes.pitch: A defensive UW deck that turns walls into a win condition. Wingmantle Chaplain and friends reward playing creatures with defender, and Walking Bulwark lets them attack. For players who enjoy an unconventional, fortress-style plan.
archetypes.rationale: Three payoffs literally count creatures with defender; Walking Bulwark turns the walls into attackers. No rare needed.

archetypes.pitch: A black deck that cheats huge threats into play from the graveyard. The Cruelty of Gix and other reanimation spells bring back premium hits like Archangel of Wrath. For players who love loading the yard and slamming bombs early.
archetypes.rationale: Four true reanimation effects plus mill to stock targets; Archangel of Wrath and Silverback Elder are premium hits.

archetypes.pitch: A RW aggro build-around centered on suiting up a creature. Astor, Bearer of Blades tutors and discounts your Equipment and Vehicles for a fast, focused clock. For players who like a lean, weaponized aggro plan.
archetypes.rationale: Astor tutors and discounts the whole package; support is real but shallow, so it is a build-around.

archetypes.pitch: A blue tempo tribe that rewards a wide, evasive board. Vodalian Hexcatcher acts as a lord and Defiler of Dreams turns your blue permanents into card draw. For players who like slippery, synergistic beatdown.
archetypes.rationale: Seven Merfolk behind a single lord; Defiler of Dreams turns blue-permanent density into a draw engine.

archetypes.pitch: A WB tribal deck that grinds value through Cleric synergies. Shadow-Rite Priest sacrifices Clerics to tutor black creatures, backed by drain and lifegain. For players who enjoy a tribal aristocrats hybrid.
archetypes.rationale: Eight Clerics behind a lord whose sac ability tutors black creatures; Evolved Sleeper becomes a Cleric on demand.

archetypes.pitch: A BR build-around that recurs and reanimates flying fatties. Rivaz of the Claw makes Dragon mana and recasts Dragons from the graveyard for relentless pressure. For players who want a big, splashy top end.
archetypes.rationale: Rivaz makes dragon mana and recasts Dragons from the graveyard; Shivan Devastator qualifies by its Dragon Hydra type line.

archetypes.pitch: A black control-midrange deck that weaponizes discard. The Raven Man makes a Bird whenever anyone discards, so symmetric wheels and hand attack all pay off. For players who like disruptive, resource-denial strategies.
archetypes.rationale: The Raven Man triggers off any player discarding, so symmetric and self-discard effects all make Birds.

archetypes.pitch: A WUB combo-control deck that animates its enchantments. Zur, Eternal Schemer turns Sagas and removal enchantments into deathtouch-lifelink threats. For players who love a controlling deck with a sneaky enchantment kill.
archetypes.rationale: Zur animates the cube's ten Sagas and removal enchantments into deathtouch-lifelink-hexproof threats sized by mana value.

archetypes.pitch: A GU tempo build-around that copies your combat tricks. Ivy, Gleeful Spellthief and Vesuvan Duplimancy double single-target spells for two-for-one blowouts. For players who like protecting one threat while piling on value.
archetypes.rationale: Both keystones copy spells that target a single creature you control, turning 14 combat tricks into two-for-ones.

archetypes.pitch: A white-based control deck that leans on planeswalkers. Urza Assembles the Titans digs for and double-activates your walkers while Plaza of Heroes supports the mana. For players who love grinding advantage with superfriends.
archetypes.rationale: The Saga digs for, deploys, and double-activates planeswalkers; five walkers plus Plaza of Heroes support it.

decks.identity: Black-green graveyard attrition: mill, surveil and discard stock the yard, then Bortuk Bonerattle and The Cruelty of Gix rebuy the threats at a discount
decks.pitch: Slot allocation (Midrange, N=40). Lands: 16 (40% of N=40) — inside the 38–42% midrange band; the deck has seven spells at MV 5+ and wants every land drop. Interaction: 6 of 24 nonland (25%) — mid-band. Threats/payoffs: 9 (37.5%) — in band. Graveyard engine/infrastructure: 9 (37.5%) — far above normal midrange engine share, justified because the engine IS the deck's requested identity: every mill/surveil/discard input feeds a rebuy output. Land modifiers: baseline 16, −0.5 for 2 producers (Deathbloom Gardener ×2), rounds back to 16 given five taplands. Projected Avg MV: 3.67.

decks.identity: Black-red midrange converting expendable bodies into cards, removal and reach via Garna and Braids
decks.pitch: Garna's two modes are timing-dependent, and the deck is built around that. Garna only draws when the dying creature was *attacking* — so deaths in combat (bad blocks forced by Splatter Goblin/Balduvian Berserker, or mid-combat sacrifices to Hurler Cyclops and Gibbering Barricade) are the draw engine, while end-step deaths (Lagomos's token, Braids's sacrifice) are pings to each opponent instead. Both modes are profitable, but when you want cards, sacrifice attackers *during* combat with an instant-speed outlet; when you just want reach, let the token expire. Note that Bone Splinters is a sorcery and never triggers Garna's draw mode.

decks.identity: White-black aristocrats draining life on every death via Elas il-Kor, with Aron converting fodder into permanent counters
decks.pitch: The legend-rule trick is a feature, not a bug. The deck runs two copies each of Elas il-Kor and Aron on purpose: with Ratadrabik of Urborg out, casting the second copy forces the legend rule, the old copy dies — draining opponents via Elas — and Ratadrabik replaces it with a non-legendary 2/2 Zombie copy that keeps its abilities. Two Elas effects draining in parallel ends games fast. The same works when Braids sacrifices a legend at end step.

decks.identity: Low-curve red-green beatdown where typed taplands over-stat Domain creatures ahead of the mana curve
decks.pitch: Slot allocation (Aggro, N=40). Lands: 14 (35% of N=40) — top of the 30–35% aggro band; kept at 14 despite the audit's formula preferring 16 because the average MV is 2.15, there are fifteen 1–2 drops, and Sprouting Goblin/Rulik Mons generate extra land value. Modifiers: −0 cantrips, −0 producers, −0 MDFC — the cut below baseline is the archetype itself. Threats: 18 of 40 (45%) — low end of the 45–55% aggro band. Interaction: 4 of 40 (10%) — low end of 10–15%. Pump: 4 slots as the aggro finisher package. Projected Avg MV: 2.15.

decks.identity: Simic kicker-value midrange with a red splash: any-color ramp and Volshe Tideturner fund kicked payoffs and X-spells
decks.pitch: Deck identity. Simic value midrange built around DMU's kicker engine. Seven any-color/ritual mana sources (2 Volshe Tideturner, 2 Salvaged Manaworker, 2 Deathbloom Gardener, 1 Llanowar Loamspeaker, plus 2 Crystal Grotto in the manabase) fund seven kicker spells (2 Joint Exploration, 2 Vineshaper Prodigy, 2 Elvish Hydromancer, 1 Vodalian Mindsinger) and two X-sinks (Silver Scrutiny, Shivan Devastator). The red splash is exactly two cards — Shivan Devastator (one R pip, cast off any-color ramp) and Vodalian Mindsinger's {1}{R} kicker — deliberately kept off the kicker ritual: Volshe Tideturner's mana only pays for instants, sorceries, and kicked spells, so Devastator is funded by the dorks and Grotto, never by Tideturner.

decks.identity: UR aggro: seven spell-cast payoff creatures pumped by 12 cheap instants; evasive damage closes by turn 5-6
decks.pitch: Deck identity. UR Prowess Aggro built around Balmor, Battlemage Captain: every instant or sorcery cast pumps the whole team +1/+0 and grants trample. Six other creatures also pay you for casting spells — Electrostatic Infantry (permanent +1/+1 counters), Ghitu Amplifier (+2/+0), Haunting Figment (unblockable) — so the 12 cheap instant-speed spells each convert into 3-8 points of extra combat damage. Nearly every threat is evasive (flying, unblockable, or Balmor-granted trample), letting damage through regardless of board state. Goldfish curve: T1 Phoenix Chick, T2 Electrostatic Infantry, T3 Balmor + 1-mana instant swings for 6+ in the air; games close by turn 5-6.

decks.strategy: WR Enlist Aggro - Soldiers & Go-Wide Tokens
decks.identity: White-red enlist aggro: token producers feed enlist attackers and go-wide pumps; Baird converts enlist attacks into more Soldiers
decks.pitch: The Baird lock. Enlist's power boost lasts "until end of turn", and Baird, Argivian Recruiter triggers "at the beginning of your end step, if you control a creature with power greater than its base power". Any enlist attack (or a Heroic Charge / Tori D'Avenant pump) therefore guarantees a Soldier every turn — the deck's engine converts combat itself into board growth.

decks.identity: Green-based five-color domain midrange: typed taplands power oversized threats, token finishers and premium domain interaction
decks.pitch: Slot allocation (Midrange, N=40). Lands: 16 (40% of N=40) — top of the midrange band; the deck wants its fifth land on time and its payoffs are land-count-driven. Interaction: 5 of 24 nonland (20.8%) — bottom edge of the 20–30% midrange band, defensible because Bite Down converts oversized threats into removal and the sideboard carries 8 more interaction pieces. Threats/payoffs: 9 (37.5%) — inside the 30–40% band. Ramp/velocity/infrastructure: 10 (41.7%) — well above a normal midrange engine share, justified by the commissioned identity: this is explicitly a Domain *Ramp* deck, and every ramp piece also advances the domain count that all payoffs read. Land modifiers: baseline 16, −0 cantrips, −0.5 for 2 mana producers (Deathbloom Gardener x2), −0 MDFC → 15.5, kept at 16 because 9 taplands make the effective untapped-land count lower. Projected Avg MV: 3.54, supported by 16 lands + 2 dorks + 5 land-fetch effects.
